issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a parameterless messageOnRide() method (interface UML and template Main use r.messageOnRide() with no arguments), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and corresponding implementations in Pig and Seal. This METHOD_PARAMETER_MISMATCH creates confusion and prevents students from matching the interface/signature expected by the exercise or the template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to use messageOnRide() with no parameters in Rideable and update Pig and Seal implementations to override messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust example usages accordingly. Prefer option A to align the solution with the stated UML and template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters that returns the phrase "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". The solution repository instead defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and Pig/Seal implement this signature and include the speed in the returned string, e.g. "Riding on Pig X at Y mph"). This is an API/identifier mismatch for the same conceptual operation (the ride message) and will cause compilation errors or confusion because the template Main calls messageOnRide() with no argument while the solution requires an int parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the speed parameter — define Rideable.messageOnRide() with no arguments and update Pig/Seal to return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"; or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and update the expected return string to include the speed. Prefer option (A) to align the solution with the original exercise specification.
